Malakul moat barray karb se laya sehra
Moat ne ibn e Hasan ka jo sajaya sehra

1
Moat ashkon ke piroye gul e faryad kahan
Khoon ki dharon ki larryon ka banaya sehra

2
Toot kar sehray ki larryan sar e maqtal bikhreen
Khak e Karbal may kalejay se lagaya sehra

3
So gaye saray barati sar e maqtal ja kar
Ghorron ki tapon ne matti may milaya sehra

4
Chunti rehti theen sada Farsh se bikhri kalian
Maa ki nazron may kuch is tarha samaya sehra

5
Baagh e jannat hua tabdeel aza khanay may
Jab farishton ne sar e arsh sunaya sehra

6
Dulha dulha ki sada aaj bhi aati hay anees
Kaisa aalam ki fizaoon may samaya sehra

from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
p = 'src/data/lyrics/mlk-almot-bre-krb-se-laia-shra.md'
old = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', 'HEAD:' + p], text=True).split('---\\n', 2)[2].strip()
_, meta, body = Path(p).read_text().split('---\\n', 2)
roman = '\\n'.join(line.removeprefix('  ') for line in meta.split('romanLyrics: |-\\n')[1].splitlines()).strip()
assert roman == old
assert [len(s.splitlines()) for s in body.strip().split('\\n\\n')] == [2, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3]
assert [s[0] for s in body.strip().split('\\n\\n')[1:]] == list('۱۲۳۴۵۶')
PY"

item.text:
Reconstructed all 14 verses in Urdu script, preserving the opening couplet and six numbered stanzas. Moved the Roman transcription unchanged into `romanLyrics`, added the Roman title, set the direction to RTL, and removed `noUrdu`.

Read “aza khanay” as عزا خانے and kept the closing “Kaisa aalam” as کیسا عالم.
